findings.title: Lift car is a floating slab with no shaft and no collider: Pip walks under it and his head comes up through the car floor
findings.problem: The lift car is the last machine in the job and where the win happens, but it is modelled as a 2.6 × 0.12 × 2.2 m plate. It hangs at y 1.12 m with two thin side panels. Nothing is under it: no pit, no shaft frame, no guide rails and no posts at the car corners. It has no physics collider. The only uprights are two 0.2 m posts at x 10.6 and 13.4, 1.3 m behind the car at z −8.3. At the game camera it reads as a hovering table or desk (lunch-models-40, -53). Pip can walk straight into its footprint. walkTo(12,−7.2) ends at (12.0,−6.91) with no stall, and his helmet and face poke up through the car floor (lunch-models-97, -98). That is a clear interpenetration in the room where the job ends. It also breaks the scale and reading of the machine: a lift should look like it rises inside something, and the tray should visibly ride it up.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:101-103 (posts at x 10.6/13.4 z −8.3, beam y 3.6, car = rbox 2.6×.12×2.2 + 2 panels, no solid())
findings.fix:
In buildLift() (src/lunch-runtime.ts:100-106):
(1) Build a shaft. Add four corner guide posts box(.12,3.7,.12) at (10.65|13.35, 1.85, −8.15|−5.85) in DMETAL, joined at the top by a frame box(2.9,.18,2.5) at y 3.6. Add a toon('#c7ccd6') back panel at z −8.2 so the car reads as sitting inside a cage.
(2) Under the car, add a pit or ground sill: rbox(2.8,.1,2.4,.04) at y .05, with hazard-stripe decal edges on three sides.
(3) Give the car a skirt: box(2.6,.35,.06) under the front edge, and front corner posts box(.08,1.1,.08) at (±1.26, .6, 1.06) so it reads as a car rather than a plate.
(4) Add one fixed collider for the shaft footprint, solid(game,2.8,2.6,2.4,12,1.3,−7), so Pip can't stand under the car. The tray is kinematic and unaffected. The hazard-stripe floor decal at z −5.9…−5.45 (decor.ts:179) stays as the threshold.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/h.mjs. walkTo(12,−7.2) must stall at z ≥ −5.7, and lunch-models-97/98 must show no head through the car. Retake lunch-models-40 and -53: the lift should read as a cage and car, not a table. g.audit(.02) must still return [].
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. I teleported Pip to (12,−3.4) and walked him to (12,−7.2): the walk reported arrived=true and ended at (12.0, 0.77, −6.91), inside the car footprint (x 10.7–13.3, z −8.1…−5.9). His helmet comes up through the car floor (verify-lunch-models-03). The code matches the finding: lunch-runtime.ts:101-103 builds two posts at z −8.3 plus a 2.6×.12×2.2 car with two panels and no solid(), and line 298 puts the car at y 1.12+h×2.5. At the game camera the lift reads as a desk (verify-lunch-models-02 survey). The fix is sound. A collider at z −8.2…−5.8 does not touch the test's cap-dock spot (11.3,−4.4) or the winch port (12,−4.8) in tests/lunch.spec.ts:26,39, and the kinematic tray is unaffected.
extra_evidence: tests/lunch.spec.ts:26,39 (cart parked at 11.3,−4.4, outside the proposed collider)
findings.fix_correction: The fix is correct as written. One addition: the stray socket box from finding 9 sits at (12,.25,−6), inside the proposed shaft collider, so hide or remove it in the same change.

findings.title: The baked tray glides through mid-air for 3 m between the end of the conveyor and the lift car
findings.problem: The conveyor group is centred at x 3.5 with an 8.5 m belt, so it ends at x 7.75. The lift car's near edge is at x 10.7. The runtime moves the tray linearly with x = −0.5 + along×12.5 up to x 12, at a fixed y 1.18. So for the last quarter of transport the tray slides through empty air: through the wall gap, over the lift-room floor, about 1.1 m up, with nothing under it (lunch-models-94, -95). This is the payoff beat of the clean run ('send the tray up'), and it reads as a bug. It also hides the idea that the conveyor delivers onto the lift.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:92 (conveyor at x 3.5, rbox 8.5 long → x −0.75…7.75)
findings.fix: Extend the belt into the lift room. In buildKitchen(), add a second conveyor section in the lift room: rbox(2.4,.25,.9,.1) at (9.5,.95,−7) with a matching belt plane box(2.4,.03,.75) sharing this.belt's texture (offset x so it scrolls in sync), plus two leg pairs at x 8.6 and 10.4. Add solid(g,2.4,.3,.9,9.5,.95,−7). Alternatively, clamp the tray path: x = min(7.6, −.5 + along×8.1) while along < 1, then hand the tray to the lift car with a short 0.4 s hop tween (x 7.6 → 12, y arcs to 1.4) once the car is down. Either way the tray must never be over bare floor.
findings.verify: Re-run lunch-models/g.mjs (tray at transport .78) and retake lunch-models-94/95: there should be belt under the tray at every transport value from 0 to 1. Also replay tests/lunch.spec.ts 'intended Lunch Rush solution' and confirm it still delivers.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. With job.tray='conveyor' and transport .78, the tray sits at (9.25, 1.18, −7) (v1 output). That is past the belt end at x 7.75 (lunch-runtime.ts:92: group at x 3.5, 8.5 m rbox) and past the lift-divider gap. In verify-lunch-models-05 it hangs over bare lift-room floor with nothing under it. Line 278 sets x = −.5 + along×12.5, which runs up to 12.
findings.fix_correction: If you extend the belt, also extend the clutter lane at lunch.ts:26 from [7.6,−7] to [10.6,−7], so clutter can't spawn on the new section. The belt has to pass through the lift-divider doorway (lunch.ts:37-38 leaves z −7.85…−6.15 open); a 0.9 m belt at z −7 fits.

findings.title: The lift winch is not connected to the lift: no rope runs from the drum to the car
findings.problem: The winch is the device the start-up kick lesson is about (3 bars running, a 9-bar kick, the capacitor cart). It is a yellow drum on a base at (13.3, −4.8), facing −x. The lift rope is a separate 2.5 cm ink cylinder from the beam straight down to the car at (12, −7.4). Nothing links the drum to the beam, a pulley or the car (lunch-models-57, -53, -40). When the player switches the lift on, the car rises but the drum doesn't turn and no rope reels in. The machine the player just powered doesn't visibly do the lifting. That weakens DR-47 (the device shows its state) and the cause-and-effect reading of the climax. The drum has no rope wound on it either, so it reads as a yellow barrel on a stand.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:104-105 (winch group at 13.3,−4.8: base, drum cyl .4×.9, two cheeks; nothing animated)
findings.fix:
In buildLift():
(1) Wrap the drum. Add 4–5 ink torus rings, TorusGeometry(.41,.025,6,24), spaced along the drum axis, plus a thin rope-coloured cylinder cyl(.42,.42,.7) in '#8a6a4a' so it reads as wound rope.
(2) Add a pulley wheel cyl(.18,.18,.08,'z') on the beam at (12.9, 3.5, −8.3).
(3) Draw the rope in two TubeGeometry segments, rebuilt only when the car moves: one from the drum top (13.3, 1.25, −4.8) up to the pulley, and one from the pulley down to the car attachment (12, carY+.6, −7.4). Replace the current liftRope cylinder.
(4) Keep a reference to the drum mesh. In render(), when powered('lift'), rotate it: drum.rotation.x −= dt×3.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-53 and -57 and the lunch-play-c19 lift-mid frame: a continuous rope from the drum over the pulley to the car is visible at the game camera, and the drum turns while the car rises (diff two frames 0.2 s apart around the drum).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code and screenshots. liftRope is one cylinder at (12,·,−7.4) running from the beam to the car (lunch-runtime.ts:103, :298). The winch group at (13.3,−4.8) is a static base, drum and cheeks (:104-105). render() never touches the drum. lunch-models-57 and -53 show a bare yellow drum with no rope and nothing linking it to the car. I'm keeping P1 because the winch is the load the start-up-kick lesson is about: DR-47 asks that the device show its own state, and nothing on the winch shows that it is running.

findings.title: Supply cart A tips onto its side (≈56°) when Pip walks past it
findings.problem: I walked Pip from near the rack (−14.2, 5) to (−12, 1.6), the natural path from the power room to the splitters. Cart A was shoved 1.8 m and left leaning on the storeroom wall at 55.9° tilt: pos (−13.16, 0.80, 1.17). It stayed tipped after 2 s (lunch-models-99b; j.mjs log: 'tilt after 2 55.6', 'settled 55.9'). The cart is one of the two power sources the whole job is built on. Tipped, its gauge face points at the wall and its outlets aim at the ceiling, and it reads as broken. The respawn rule (game.ts:342) only fires above y 2.1, so it never rights itself. It is a 40 kg box collider 1.7 × 1.3 × 1.1 with its centre of mass at mid-height. Pip's controller can lever it over against the wall lip.
evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:163-168 (model sits low on wheels, but the collider COM is at the box centre)
findings.fix: Lock pitch and roll on wheeled carts. Where props are created (game.ts prop body setup), for kinds supply, capcart and dolly set body.setEnabledRotations(false,true,false,true), so they can spin about Y but never tip. Also lower their centre of mass with setAdditionalMassProperties so the COM is about 0.3 m above the floor. As a fallback, extend the respawn check at game.ts:342: if an id'd prop's up-vector y < 0.6 for 3 s, set it upright at its current x/z with a dust puff (this also covers DR-15).
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/j.mjs: 'tilt settled' must be < 5°. Retake lunch-models-99b: cart upright, gauge readable. tests/lunch.spec.ts must still pass.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it exactly. Walking from (−13.83,5) to (−12,1.6) leaves cart A at 55.6° tilt, which settles at 55.9° at (−13.16,0.79,1.16). Cart B stays at 0°. In verify-lunch-models-06 the cart leans on the storeroom wall with its wheels in the air. walkTo moves in a straight line through the cart's footprint, but a player taking the same line would hit it the same way. game.ts:342 respawns only when y>2.1. The heavy-carry code (game.ts:331) zeroes angular velocity but never restores rotation, so even picking the cart up leaves it tipped. That breaks the forgiving-interaction rule.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:331 (heavy carry sets angvel 0 but never resets rotation)
findings.fix_correction: The fix is correct (Rapier's RigidBody.setEnabledRotations(x,y,z,wakeUp) exists). It is simplest to apply it when the prop's body is built for kinds supply, capcart and dolly. Also reset the rotation upright in the heavy-carry branch at game.ts:331, so grabbing any heavy prop rights it.

findings.title: Job-item yellow (#ffc94d) is used by decorative clutter: 9 crates, 12 mugs and a crate right beside the bridges; teal and white crates too
findings.problem: Lunch's job items are all #ffc94d: the wedge, bridges, splitters, thick cable, kitchen post and mop wringer. But the clutter palette in lunch.ts:18 includes '#ffc94d', and the mug prefab defaults to '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:12). From the live prop dump, 9 crates and 4 clutter mugs are job yellow. Examples: a box at (0.32, 8.25) beside the wedge and mop route, a box at (14.88, 6.97) next to the bridges, and boxes at (−13, −8.39) and (−15.35, −7.52) in the storeroom right where the player hunts for the capacitor cart. The 8 kitchen mugs placed by lunch.ts:14 are also job yellow, in a perfect row across the two counters. In lunch-models-76 a yellow crate sits a metre from the yellow bridge ramps, and in -37 and -38 the eight yellow mugs are the most saturated shapes in the kitchen. A first-time player can't tell yellow-means-use-me apart from noise. That breaks DR-45 and the grab-prompt flow: the prompt says 'Grab the mug' at the post (lunch-models-34). The same palette adds 6 teal '#5f8fa8' crates and 7 white '#e9f0f2' crates. Cardboard should stay kraft (DR-51, 'no teal boxes').
evidence: src/levels/lunch.ts:14 (8 mugs with no colour → prefab default)
findings.fix:
(1) In src/levels/lunch.ts:18, change the colors to kraft and neutral families only, for example ['#c98f5a','#d7a56d','#e0b47a','#b8b0a2','#9fb0c4']. Boxes then stay cardboard, and mugs and carts take a neutral.
(2) In src/levels/clutter.ts, stop passing the cluster colour to 'box' items; boxes always pick from FLOOR kraft. Only carts, mugs and beanbags take the level accents.
(3) Change the mug prefab default in src/props/prefabs.ts:12 to a non-job colour ('#f4efe6' white with a '#e5484d' band). Give lunch.ts:14 mugs explicit mixed colours ['#f4efe6','#e5484d','#3f7fd6','#6cc58a'].
(4) Add a unit test: for every level's clutter output, no non-id prop colour is within ΔE 25 of #ffc94d or #ffc629.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/a.mjs and check props.json: the only #ffc94d entries are id'd job items. Retake lunch-models-02 survey and -37: the yellow shapes are exactly the wedge, bridges, splitters, post, thick cable and mop wringer.
findings.verify_reason: The live prop dump matches the finding exactly: box|#ffc94d 9, mug|#ffc94d 4, 8 mugs with no colour (the prefab default #ffc94d, prefabs.ts:12), box|#5f8fa8 6, box|#e9f0f2 7. The palette at lunch.ts:18 includes #ffc94d. In the screenshots the yellow crates sit beside the bridges and the mop, and the mug row is the most saturated thing in the kitchen (lunch-models-37). There is more of it than the finding lists. Dining chair k=2 is #ffc94d (decor.ts:196). The chef-side NPC at (−6.6,−7.4) is #ffc94d (lunch.ts:32). verify-lunch-models-09 shows a 'Grab the crate' prompt on a job-yellow crate next to the dining table.
findings.fix_correction: The palette fix is fine. Also change dining chair k=2 at decor.ts:196 to a non-job colour (e.g. '#6cc58a'), and the NPC at lunch.ts:32 from '#ffc94d' to another blob colour.

findings.title: Room density is about half the rule: 137 props on a 33 × 20 m floor, half of them paper and mugs; large empty cells in the corridor and kitchen
findings.problem: The live dump counts 137 props in total (clutter max is 160). Of these, 43 are paper sheets and 24 are mugs, so 49% are tiny items that barely register at the game camera. Big readable clutter: 41 boxes, of which 10 are the scripted storeroom grid, plus 3 carts, 4 cones and 3 bins. There are no beanbags or lounge clusters, even though 'lounge' is in the recipe list, because no anchor passed the lane test. A 4 × 4 m heat-map of prop positions has many zero cells. Row z 2…6 is almost all zeros across the corridor, the kitchen centre (x −8…8, z −6…−2) has 0–3 per cell, and the lift-room column x 12…16 has 0–1. DR-67 wants at least 250 props and at least 3 per walkable 4 × 4 cell. In the survey (lunch-models-02) the wood corridor reads as a big empty floor with a mop, three bridges and two bots. AGENTS 3 calls for big dense rooms with hundreds of props. The lanes (lunch.ts:19-26) are so many and so wide (r 1.3 on long polylines crossing the whole corridor several times) that clutter can only land along the walls.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/props.json (137 props; paper 43, mug 24, box 41, cart 3, cone 4, bin 3, beanbag 0)
findings.fix:
(1) In src/levels/lunch.ts:19-22, collapse the duplicated lane polylines. Several revisit [.3,2.4]↔[.3,−1.3] and [10,1] three times. Keep one corridor spine at r 1.1 instead of 1.3, so clusters can sit between the routes and the walls.
(2) Raise max to 300. Add lunch-themed recipes in src/levels/clutter.ts: 'kitchen' (a crate of veg, a pot and a tray stack on a cart), 'lunchtable' (a small table, 2 chairs and trays), 'queue' (stanchions or a menu A-frame), and 'storage' (2–3 crate stacks, 2 high).
(3) Let the fill pass place 2-high crate stacks along the walls of the power room and lift room.
(4) Keep paper and mug litter under 20% of the count.
findings.verify: Re-run a.mjs: props ≥ 250, beanbag/lounge or the new lunch recipes present, paper+mug ≤ 20%, and the 4×4 heat-map printed by the analysis has ≥ 3 in every walkable cell. tests/lunch.spec.ts must still pass with the same route, and the lane count shouldn't regress DR-16.
findings.verify_reason: The live count is 137 props: paper 43, mugs 24, boxes 41, carts 3, cones 4, bins 3, beanbags 0. My own 4×4 m heat-map (v3) has the row at z 2…6 at 0 in almost every column, and the kitchen and lift-room cells hold 0–5. The survey (verify-lunch-models-02) shows a large empty wood corridor. That is well below AGENTS 3 (hundreds of props) and DR-67 (≥250).
findings.fix_correction: Part of the empty band is deliberate. The cleaner bots' loop perimeter (lunch-runtime.ts:22, LANE x −1…14, z 1.2…5.4) and the lift-feed cable crossings have to stay clear, or bots snag clutter and routes get blocked. Put new clusters inside the loop only away from the two bridge crossings (x≈7 and 9), and keep the lane r .9 loop lane (lunch.ts:24). Treat '≥3 per walkable cell' as excluding the painted loop band.

findings.title: Storeroom darkness is still a flat lid at y 1.5: the lamp shade at 2.2 m shines bright above it and the plane edge reads as a tinted sheet (LR1 still open)
findings.problem: The unlit storeroom is shown by an 8.9 × 10 m unlit plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8, a cut-out radial hole and depthWrite false. Everything taller than 1.5 m pokes through it fully lit. The floor lamp's shade (y 1.78–2.22) shows cream and bright while everything under the lid is violet (lunch-models-70 'lid on' vs -71 'lid off'; also the start shot -01 and survey -02). At zoom 9 inside the room, the lid only tints. Crates, the floor and Pip are clearly readable, so 'dark room, can't find things' isn't sold either. The rule that nothing in the dark storeroom can be grabbed (canGrab) then feels arbitrary, because the player can plainly see the boxes. The capacitor cart and coolbox are hidden by mesh.visible=false (lunch-runtime.ts:293) rather than by darkness, so they pop in when the room lights.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:110-111 (stand 1.8 m pole, shade at y 2 height .45)
findings.fix:
Replace the lid with per-material darkening.
(1) Add a 'storeDark' uniform to toon's onBeforeCompile (src/render/toon.ts rimShader). Multiply outgoingLight by mix(1., .28, storeDark × inBox(vWorldPosition, minX −16.5, maxX −7.75, minZ −10, maxZ 0)), with a 0.4 m smoothstep at the doorway.
(2) Tween storeDark from 1 to 0 over 0.5 s when lit() turns true.
(3) Keep the capacitor cart and coolbox visible, but darkened (they then fade in with the light instead of popping).
(4) If that is too costly, at least lower the lid to y 2.4 above everything in the room, and give the lamp shade its own dark material while the room is unlit.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-70 (unlit) and -90 (lit). In 70 the lamp shade and crate tops share the same dim value (median luma within 15). At the game camera (lunch-models-01) there must be no bright object above a dark plane. Diff lit vs unlit in a crop of the doorway for a soft edge.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. In verify-lunch-models-10 (game camera inside the storeroom), the floor-lamp shade draws bright cream above the violet lid, while the crate grid and Pip under the lid stay fully readable, just tinted. The code matches: PlaneGeometry(8.9,10) at y 1.5, opacity .8 (lunch-runtime.ts:66), and the shade at y 2 (:111). The capacitor cart and coolbox are hidden with mesh.visible (:293). RULES DR-76 already names this exact defect as open.
findings.fix_correction: Fallback (4) says 'lower the lid to y 2.4'; it means raise it. A raised lid also shows parallax at the high game camera: it spills a dark strip onto the power-room floor beyond the store-front wall (z 0…0.3), so the per-material storeDark uniform is the right fix. If the lid is raised anyway, shrink it toward −z by about 0.5 m to compensate.

findings.title: REGRESSION (LR15/DR-24): Lunch renders 1257 draw calls at start (1309 in lowfx), not the ~175 PROGRESS claims; 156 shell-wall meshes are never merged
findings.problem: snapshot().drawCalls reads 1257 at start and 1303 in survey with fullfx, and 1309 with fullfx off. PROGRESS.md's performance table lists Lunch at '~175'. game.ts:450 now counts every pass of the frame (scene and outlines), so part of the jump is the counter. But a scene traverse still finds about 534 visible meshes per pass: 42 merged decor buckets, 123 instanced prop parts, 156 meshes under the shell walls, 207 other meshes (interior walls 35, port rings, plugs, pulses, puddles, bots, lamps, blobs, Pip) and 6 sprites. The shell walls (windows: sky, 5 frame bars, sill and 6 blinds × 10; posters; wallpaper) are built on game.root via shellWall(), so freeze(decorRoot) never merges them. Separately, the portable-lamp cord TubeGeometry is disposed and rebuilt every frame, because the condition distance(lamp,post) > .3 is always true. Host fps is still 60, but DR-24's ≤ about 250 budget is blown about 5×, and this room was the one perf was fixed for.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:32-43 (shellWall on game.root), :80-82, :180 (windows), src/levels/dressing.ts:226-231 (13 meshes per window)
findings.fix:
(1) In shellWall(), split each wall into a static part (lower wainscot, rail, base) parented to decorRoot, and the folding upper group. In the upper group, merge the window units, wallpaper, cap and wall art into one mesh per material after build. Call freeze(upper) right after decorate(), since the group only changes its transform.
(2) Merge the 7 interior walls' 5 parts into one geometry per wall and material.
(3) In lunch-runtime.ts:302, rebuild the cord only when the lamp has moved more than 2 cm since the last build (store the last position).
(4) Update the PROGRESS perf table with the new counting method. Report calls per pass and total separately.
findings.verify: Re-run lunch-models/a.mjs and i.mjs: snapshot().drawCalls ≤ 500 total (≤ 250 per pass) at start and survey, shell meshes ≤ 20, fps unchanged. tools/perf.mjs on lunch gives p95 ≤ the PROGRESS value.
findings.verify_reason: The measurement holds. drawCalls is 1303 at start and in survey with fullfx, and 1341 with fullfx off. A traverse of visible meshes gives {inDecor 42, inst 123, shell 156, other 207} = 528 per pass, over the ~250 budget even counted per pass. The portable-lamp cord geometry uuid changes every frame (v1: 'cord same geom false'; the lamp is 9 m from the post, so lunch-runtime.ts:302 always rebuilds it). Calling it a 'regression' overstates it: commit 19deb71 changed snapshot().drawCalls to count every pass, while PROGRESS.md:410 (~175) was measured with the old last-pass counter. Fps stays at 60 on the host and no player-facing slowdown was measured, so P2, not P1.

findings.title: Lunch floors still read too bright, and the pale thin leads barely separate from the concrete (DR-54 known, LR5 partial)
findings.problem: Median floor luma in the start shot: power-room concrete 201, corridor wood 191, kitchen tiles 197. Survey: wood 192, tiles 211. The rule's band is 140–185, and the concept floors measure 152–175. ?norim gives the same numbers (concrete 201, wood 191), so the new rim light is not the cause. The bright floors flatten the room: the white fridge, white crates, cream lamp shades, thin cables and white blob chef all sit within about 20 luma of the floor. The thin leads are now 7.5 cm hoses in '#ffe2a8' with ink outlines (better than the old hairlines). Sampled across a lead on the power-room concrete at zoom 9, the cable body is about 213–228 against a floor of about 190–206, roughly 15–20 luma apart, so the cable mostly reads by its outline (lunch-models-15, -99b). At the game camera the outline thins, and the thin leads crossing the kitchen tiles nearly vanish (lunch-models-37, -38: the long grey line across the kitchen). The cable is supposed to be the star (AGENTS 4, DR-53).
evidence: luma measurements (PIL) on mockups/review5/shots/lunch-models-01-start.jpg and -11-norim-start.png: concrete 201, wood 191, tiles 197
findings.fix:
(1) Darken the Lunch floor bases in src/levels/decor.ts:175-178: concrete '#cbbfa8' → '#ada28c', wood '#d9ab6e' → '#c0925a', kitchen tiles '#f4ecd8'/'#8fcac0' → '#e2d8c2'/'#7fb8ae'. Target medians: concrete about 170, wood about 165, tiles about 175.
(2) Give thin cables a saturated identity instead of near-white: THIN '#ffe2a8' → '#ff9f45' (orange extension lead), keeping the strain ramp while held. Or keep the cream and add ink bands every 0.6 m like the thick cable, but thinner.
(3) Re-measure after the change.
findings.verify: PIL crops of retaken lunch-models-01 and -11 (norim): floor medians 150–185. Thin-cable body vs floor at the game camera ≥ 40 luma apart, or chroma clearly above the floor in a 400×400 crop around Pip mid-drag (DR-53).
findings.verify_reason: My PIL measurements on verify-lunch-models-01: concrete medians 185 and 202, wood 192, tiles 191. Survey: wood 192, tiles 218. Most of these are above DR-54's 140–185 band (DR-54 already lists 'Lunch wood 193'). A pixel row across the thin lead near Pip reads cable 208–237 against floor 195–202, with only the ink outline dipping to 161–172, so the lead reads mainly by its outline.
findings.fix_correction: Don't recolour THIN to orange '#ff9f45'. The overheat tint WARM is '#ffa04a' (lunch-runtime.ts:10, applied at :318), and an orange-glowing cable is the room's signal that a thin lead is overloaded (the kitchen-post lesson). Orange leads would hide that warning. Darken the floors (part 1) and keep the leads cream with thin ink bands, or use a hue far from the heat ramp and the cyan port rings (e.g. a saturated blue '#4f8fe8'), then re-measure.

findings.title: A stray default 'target socket' box sits under the lift car at (12, 0.25, −6), with no purpose and no collider
findings.problem: Game always builds the generic target ring and a 0.48 × 0.38 × 0.3 dark socket box at level.target. Lunch's target is {x:12, z:−6}. LunchRuntime hides game.target (the ring) but not the socket box. A dark featureless cube therefore sits on the lift-room floor right in front of the lift, between the hazard stripe and the car. It looks like a job object (a socket or a battery), Pip walks straight through it (lunch-models-97), and it is visible in every lift-room shot (lunch-models-53, -57, -94). This is a false affordance (DR-17) at the most important station of the room.
evidence: src/game.ts:87-88 (target torus + socket BoxGeometry(.48,.38,.3) toon('#384454') at level.target)
src/lunch-runtime.ts:42 (hides ropeMesh, plug, target, screen; not the socket)
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:88, keep a reference (this.targetSocket=socket). In the LunchRuntime constructor (lunch-runtime.ts:42), add game.targetSocket.visible=false. Station and hub levels already skip it. Alternatively, skip building the socket when level.id==='lunch'.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-53 and -97: no dark cube under the lift. The e.mjs mesh listing near (11,−5.6) no longer contains the 384454 box.
findings.verify_reason: Live scene query: a visible BoxGeometry in material 384454 at (12,0.25,−6). game.ts:88 builds it, and game.ts:92 hides it only for station and hub levels. lunch-runtime.ts:42 hides target but not the socket. It shows as a dark cube in front of the lift in verify-lunch-models-03 and -05, and in lunch-models-57.

findings.title: Posters collide with windows and with each other: the plant poster on the store window, the graph poster on the lift window, the sun and bolt posters overlapping by 12 cm at the same depth
findings.problem:
Three wall-art placements in lunch() ignore the window grid and each other.
(a) Back wall 'plant' poster at x −8.5. The window at x −7.9 spans −9.1…−6.7, so the poster is mounted on top of the glass and blinds. In lunch-models-70 and -90 it floats over the window slats.
(b) Back wall 'graph' poster at x 15.2, over the window at x 14.5 (13.3…15.7). It sits on the blinds in lunch-models-97 and -53.
(c) Side wall 'sun' at local x −3 (world z 3.0, width 0.72 → z 2.64…3.36) and 'bolt' at local x −3.6 (z 3.24…3.96). They overlap by 0.12 m, and both frames are at local z .16, so the overlap strip is coplanar and z-fights. Both are also behind the storeroom rack's crates and upright at x −15.8 (lunch-models-72).
Posters should be mounted on clear wall (DR-72), and coplanar overlaps flicker (DR-77).
findings.fix:
In src/levels/decor.ts lunch():
(1) Move 'plant' to a pier between windows, e.g. x −9.5 (between the windows at −11.1 and −7.9: piers at −9.9…−9.1, width 0.8). Scale it 0.7 so it fits, or move it to the storeroom divider face.
(2) Move 'graph' to the pier at x 12.9 (between 11.3 and 14.5), at scale 0.7.
(3) Separate the side-wall posters. Put 'sun' at local x −1.6 (z 1.6, above the splitter shelf area) and 'bolt' at local x −8.6. Keep both clear of the rack span z 3.3…6.7 and the cork board at z 7.05…8.55.
(4) Add an assert helper wallArtFits(x,w) that rejects art overlapping windowXs ± 1.25 or other art.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-72 (orbit to the side wall) and -90: no poster touches a window frame or another poster. Take two zoom-9 frames 0.1 s apart on the side wall: the diff there should be zero.
findings.verify_reason: All three placements check out. The plant poster sits on the storeroom window blinds (verify-lunch-models-10, top right). The window at −7.9 is still built via windowUnit at decor.ts:180, and dressing.ts:28 makes windows 2.4 wide. The graph poster sits on the lift-room window (verify-lunch-models-03). The sun and bolt posters overlap on the side wall (verify-lunch-models-11): sun spans −3.36…−2.64 and bolt −3.96…−3.24 (wallArt width .72, dressing.ts:46), both at z .16, so the frames are coplanar. I didn't capture flicker across frames, but the coplanar overlap is confirmed in code.
findings.fix_correction: Don't move 'graph' to x 12.9. That pier is directly behind the lift car's back panel (car x 10.7–13.3, panel 1.1 m tall at z −8.1, posts at 13.4), so the poster would be hidden behind the lift. Use the strip past the last window instead (x≈16.1, clear span 15.75…16.37) at scale .6, or put it on the lift-divider face.

findings.title: Power-room wall rack: an upright runs through two stock crates, the crates overhang the plank front, the rack has no collider, and it is built twice
findings.problem: The rack group is at (−16.1, 0, 5), rotated π/2. Its uprights are at local (±1.6, z .3) → world (−15.8, z 3.4) and (−15.8, z 6.6). Its planks span world x −16.25…−15.75. The decorative crates (rbox .6) are at x −15.8, z 3.6/4.7/5.8, y 1.3 and 2.4. So the crate at (−15.8, 1.3, 3.6) spans z 3.3…3.9 and the upright at z 3.36…3.44 runs straight through it. The same goes for the crate at y 2.4, whose bottom at 2.15 is under the upright top at 2.2. Every crate centre sits 0.2 m in front of the plank centre, so 0.25 m of each crate hangs past the plank's front edge (lunch-models-01, -72: upper crates look perched on nothing). F11 from ART is still open: the rack is decor-only, with no solid(), so physics props can't rest on or bump it, and the audit can't see it. lunch-runtime.ts:129 builds a second, identical rack (same group, transform and parts) on decorRoot. That doubles geometry and outlines for no benefit.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:189-190 (rack + 6 crates at x −15.8, z 3.6+(k%3)*1.1, y 1.3/2.4)
findings.fix:
(1) Delete the duplicate rack at src/lunch-runtime.ts:129.
(2) In decor.ts:189-190, move the uprights to the plank ends: local sx ±1.66, local z −.13 and +.33 (front and back pairs, 4 posts in total). Put the crates at z 3.75, 5.0 and 6.25, so none is within 0.35 m of an upright. Set the crate x to −16.0 (the plank centre) so they sit fully on the planks.
(3) Add solid(game,.5,.08,3.4,−16.0,1.0,5) and solid(game,.5,.08,3.4,−16.0,2.1,5) for the planks, plus solid() for each crate, so the audit and props see them.
(4) Rack crates use kraft colours only (see the yellow/teal finding).
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-72 and a zoom-9 crop at (−15.8, 1.3, 3.6): no upright through a crate, and every crate's bottom face sits fully on a plank. An extended audit (fixed-vs-fixed overlap or a decor bounds check) reports no intersections for the rack. The scene mesh count drops by the rack's 4 parts.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry checks out. Uprights are at world (−15.8, z 3.4/6.6); crate k=0/3 spans z 3.3–3.9, so the upright passes through it. Planks span x −16.25…−15.75 while crates span −16.1…−15.5, so each crate overhangs the plank front by 0.25 m. verify-lunch-models-11 shows the right upright running through a crate and the crates perched on the plank edge. lunch-runtime.ts:129 repeats decor.ts:189 part for part, so the rack is built twice. There is no solid() for it.

findings.title: Corridor and dining furniture have no colliders: Pip walks into the benches and plants, the bench blobs stand inside the benches, and the pink blob is inside a dining chair
findings.problem:
The corridor benches (decor.ts:194), the three potted plants (decor.ts:197) and the three dining chairs (decor.ts:196) are decor meshes with no solid(). The table (195) and the vending and cooler (192-193) do have colliders.
- walkTo(−4.2, 10.2) from (−4.2, 8.4) ends at z 9.5 with Pip standing inside the bench seat (lunch-models-74).
- walkTo(−7.2, 1.0) from (−7.2, 2.6) walks into the plant at (−7.2, 1.2): Pip and the pot share space (lunch-models-75, -80).
- The 'hungry lunch crowd' blobs at (−3.8, 9) and (−2.4, 8.9) (lunch.ts:30) have r ≈ .33 and the bench seats span z 9.225…9.675, so the blobs stand in the benches' front edge instead of sitting on them (lunch-models-73, -01).
- The pink blob at (14.5, 9.1) (lunch.ts:31) is 0.64 m from the k=0 dining chair at (14.21, 8.53). The chair's half-diagonal of 0.39 plus the blob's 0.33 gives 0.72 > 0.64, so they interpenetrate (lunch-models-76).
The layout audit only checks props, NPCs and fixed colliders, so all of this passes g.audit() = [].
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/e.mjs output ('bench walk-through end … z 9.5', 'plant walk end … z 0.944')
findings.fix:
(1) In decor.ts lunch(), add colliders: solid(game,1.3,.5,.45,x,.25,9.45) per bench; solid(game,.52,.9,.52,x,.45,z) per plant; and solid(game,.55,.9,.55,cx,.45,cz,−a−π/2) per dining chair.
(2) Seat the crowd: set seated:true on the two bench blobs, at (−4.2, 9.45) and (−2.6, 9.45) with yaw π (facing the room and camera). Move the pink blob to (15.3, 9.3) or seat it on chair k=0.
(3) Extend game.audit() to also test NPC balls against decor bounding boxes (traverse decorRoot before freeze()), so this class of overlap is caught.
findings.verify: Re-run e.mjs: the bench walk stalls at z ≤ 9.0 and the plant walk stalls at z ≥ 1.6. Retake lunch-models-73 and -76: blobs sit on the benches and don't intersect chairs. The extended audit returns [].
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. The bench walk ends at z 9.5, with Pip inside the bench seat (verify-lunch-models-07), where the blue blob also stands in the bench's front edge. The plant walk ends at (−7.2, 1.146), inside the pot at (−7.2,1.2). decor.ts:194, 196 and 197 have no solid(). The pink blob at (14.5,9.1) is 0.64 m from chair k=0 at (14.21,8.53), less than the 0.72 m of combined extents, and they visibly overlap in verify-lunch-models-09.
extra_evidence: v2.mjs output: 'bench walk end z 9.5', 'plant walk end z 1.146'

findings.title: Dining chairs float on a single stalk with no foot, and the corridor plants use a different model from the prop plants
findings.problem: Each dining chair is a seat rbox at y .48, a back and one 3 cm pole cyl(.03,.03,.4) centred at y .26, so it runs from 0.06 to 0.46. The pole stops 6 cm above the floor and there is no base, so each chair hovers on a stalk (lunch-models-76: the yellow and blue chairs have a thin black stalk and no foot). The chairs are also single flat slabs with no cushion or edge detail, which is thinner than the office chair prefab (prefabs.ts:66-76) used in other rooms. Separately, the decor plants are three spheres on a pot (decor.ts:197), while the clutter plant prefab uses icosahedra (prefabs.ts:84-86). The room therefore has two visibly different plant styles side by side (lunch-models-77).
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:196 (chair: seat .48, back, cyl(.03,.03,.4) at y .26)
findings.fix:
(1) In decor.ts:196, replace the chair with a café chair: a seat rbox(.5,.08,.5,.08) at .46; a back rbox(.46,.42,.07,.08) at .74, z −.22, tilted −.1; four legs box(.04,.44,.04) at (±.2, .22, ±.2) in INK; and a pad rbox(.4,.03,.4,.08) in a lighter tint. Or use makeProp('chair') with the level's colours.
(2) In decor.ts:197, build the corridor plants with makeProp('plant') (static clones), so the room has one plant language.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 retake of lunch-models-76: every chair touches the floor at four legs, with no gap under the pole. Corridor plants match the clutter plants in lunch-models-77.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code. The dining-chair stalk cyl(.03,.03,.4) at y .26 runs from 0.06 to 0.46, with no base (decor.ts:196). The corridor plants are sphere clusters (decor.ts:197) while the prefab plant uses ico (prefabs.ts:84-86). Both plant styles appear together in verify-lunch-models-09 (sphere plant at the lower left). At the game camera the 6 cm gap is hard to see, and the stalk mostly reads as a thin black pole in lunch-models-76, so the visual effect is minor.

findings.title: Copy-paste layouts and office props in the kitchen: a 10-box grid, 8 mugs and 8 papers in a ruler-straight row, and keyboards, mice and cable tails on kitchen counters
findings.problem: lunch.ts:13 places 10 identical cartons in an exact 3-column grid at 0.9 × 0.8 m pitch in the storeroom (lunch-models-61, -63, -02). It reads as a spreadsheet, not storage. lunch.ts:14 places 8 mugs and 8 papers at an exact 0.42 m pitch along the two kitchen 'desks' (lunch-models-37, -38). The desks are the office desk prefab, and deskClutter() adds a textured keyboard, a mouse, a pencil cup or lamp and an ink cable tail to each (prefabs.ts:40-50, 65). The kitchen's serving counter therefore reads as an office workstation: in lunch-models-37 the counters show keyboards next to the mug row. DR-67 asks for varied clusters, not grids, and DR-61 asks that props read as what they are (a serving counter or pass).
evidence: src/levels/lunch.ts:11,14 (2 desks, 8 mugs and 8 papers at i*.42)
findings.fix:
(1) Storeroom: replace the grid loop with 3 hand-placed stacks (2 high, ±0.25 rad yaw jitter, ±0.08 m offsets) plus 2 singles. Keep the crate pile only where it blocks nothing (z ≤ −3.2 still keeps the door lane clear).
(2) Add a 'counter' prop kind or variant: a rbox(1.6,.95,.7) stainless top '#c7ccd6' over a base with 2 doors and pulls, with no deskClutter. Or pass variant −1 to skip deskClutter for kitchen desks.
(3) Replace the mug and paper rows with 3–4 stacked tray piles, a cutlery cup, a napkin box and 4 plates, at jittered spacing (±0.06 m) and mixed colours.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-37, -61 and -02: no exact rows or grids are visible, and the kitchen counter shows no keyboards or mice. A first-look naming of the counter in the norim start shot reads as 'kitchen counter'.
findings.verify_reason: lunch.ts:13 lays out an exact 3-column grid, visible as a carton grid in verify-lunch-models-10. lunch.ts:14 places mugs and papers at an exact 0.42 m pitch. The desk prefab always calls deskClutter (prefabs.ts:65). lunch-models-37 shows keyboards beside the yellow mug row on the kitchen counters.

findings.title: Capacitor cart reads as paint cans next to a black box, and has no visible inlet socket for the lead the player must plug into it
findings.problem: The capacitor cart is the 'aha' object of the room: the lift's feed plugs into it, and it supplies the start-up kick. Its model is four plain blue cylinders with grey caps on a cart deck, plus an INK rbox (.36 × .5 × .85) with a thin green light strip. In lunch-models-90 and -91 (storeroom lit) the cylinders read as paint or chemical drums, and the ink block reads as a dark hole, because its 0.85 × 0.5 m face is untrimmed. Nothing says 'capacitor': no sleeve stripe with − marks, no top vent cross and no terminals. The model has no socket plate either. The inlet port 'cap' is just a floating cyan ring at the cart's position + 0.75 m (lunch-runtime.ts:54), so the player plugs a cable into thin air on the deck. Every other inlet (oven, fridge, post, winch, conveyor motor) has a socketPlate().
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:72 (socketPlate helper used for the other inlets)
findings.fix:
In prefabs.ts capcart:
(1) For each can, add a darker sleeve stripe, box(.08,.6,.02) in '#1f4f9a', with 3 small white '−' boxes (.05 × .012).
(2) Add a top vent cross of two box(.3,.01,.03) parts in INK on each grey cap.
(3) Add two terminal posts cyl(.03,.03,.06) on each cap.
(4) Replace the ink block with a control box rbox(.36,.5,.85) in DMETAL, with an ink face panel, a green 'charged' lamp sphere and a charge gauge decal.
(5) Add a socket plate (the same geometry as lunch-runtime socketPlate) on the box's +x face at local (.74, .45, 0).
In lunch-runtime.ts:54, set the lift so the ring sits at the plate (lift .45 relative to the body centre).
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-91 and -85 at zoom 9: a viewer can name it as 'big capacitors' (striped cans with vents) and sees a socket where the cable goes. Retake lunch-play-c17 (cap fed): the plug end sits on the plate.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code. The 'cap' port has only a floating ring with lift .75 and no socketPlate (lunch-runtime.ts:54), while every other inlet calls socketPlate (:78, 82, 86, 95, 105). The capcart model is 4 plain cylinders plus an INK rbox (prefabs.ts:169-172). In lunch-models-91 they read as blue drums with white lids. That 'paint cans' reading is my subjective call, but the missing socket is objective.

findings.title: Still open: the vending machine is a slab with a sticker grid, the water cooler is a box with a can on it, and the supply-cart gauge is a bare board from behind
findings.problem:
These were reported in research-art F14/F15 and are re-checked here.
- The vending machine (decor.ts:192) is now correctly facing +z (LR2 fixed). But it is still a red rbox with a pale window holding 9 coloured squares. There is no header sign, coin/keypad panel, dispense flap or kick plate, and its 1 × 2 m red face carries no trim (lunch-models-74, -01). DR-62 says a fixture should show at least 6 cues and no flat face over 0.5 m² without trim.
- The water cooler (decor.ts:193) is a white box with a blue cylinder: no bottle neck, no taps, no drip tray, no cup holder (lunch-models-74).
- The supply carts' gauges are Gauge.mount boxes (kit.ts:108): an ink 0.63 × 0.41 board with the dial decal on the front only. From behind or the side they are a thin black plank on the yellow body (lunch-models-72, -01). The research flagged this (research-art-08). The two INK outlet cylinders on the end face read as a pair of eyes (lunch-models-99b, -72), so the cart reads like a face, which competes with the blobs.
evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:163-168 (supply: two INK cyl outlets at w*.44)
findings.fix:
(1) Vending (decor.ts:192): add a header box(1.0,.25,.06) with a canvas 'SNACKS' glyph decal; a keypad panel rbox(.22,.5,.04) at x +.33 with a 3×4 button grid and a coin slot; a dispense flap rbox(.66,.2,.04) at y .25 in INK; a kick plate box(1,.12,.04); and side trim strips.
(2) Cooler (decor.ts:193): change the bottle to a cyl(.2,.2,.45) plus a neck cyl(.07,.07,.1). Add two taps (red and blue cyl(.03,.03,.06,'z')) at y .9, a drip tray box(.3,.03,.12), and a cup tube on the side.
(3) Gauge.mount (kit.ts:108): add a housing, a rbox back shell (.72s × .5s × .1) in DMETAL behind the board, and a short post or stem to the cart top.
(4) Supply outlets: replace the two bare INK cylinders with a socketPlate-style faceplate (cream rbox .38×.38 with two ink holes), so they read as sockets, not eyes.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 crops after the change, front and 180° orbit of the vending machine, cooler and supply cart (lunch-models-74, -72, -16): ≥ 6 cues on the vending machine, a finished gauge back, and the supply end face naming as 'sockets'.
findings.verify_reason: verify-lunch-models-07 shows the vending machine as a red slab with a 3×3 sticker window, and the cooler as a box with a blue cylinder (decor.ts:192-193). verify-lunch-models-11 shows cart B's gauge from behind as a bare black board (kit.ts:108 builds the box and a front decal only), and the two INK outlet cylinders on its end face read as a pair of eyes.

findings.title: Kitchen set dressing is under-modelled: pots are bare cylinders and the oven's hood and back are large flat untrimmed slabs
findings.problem: The four pots on the prep table (decor.ts:186) are plain cylinders cyl(.16,.14,.22) in red and grey. With no rims, handles or lids, they read as tin cans or cups (lunch-models-33, -59). The oven has good front cues: window, three knobs, bake gauge and socket. But from the side and back (lunch-models-31) the 2.6 × 1.7 m body and the 2.8 × 1.5 m hood top are uniform flat faces: no panel lines, vents, feet or back panel. The chimney is a plain cylinder going into the void above the wall line. The player orbits (AGENTS 8), and DR-62/63 require trimmed faces under 0.5 m² and finished backs. The baked-tray model is a red rbox with three squashed spheres (prefabs.ts:156), which reads as buns on a tray and is fine.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:75 (oven rbox 2.6×1.7×1.3, hood box 2.8×.35×1.5, chimney cyl .25×1.1)
findings.fix:
(1) Pots: for each, add a TorusGeometry(.16,.015) rim in METAL, two handle boxes box(.06,.03,.03) at ±.19, and on two of the four a lid cyl(.165,.165,.03) with a knob sphere(.03).
(2) Oven: add a side panel inset rbox(1.1,1.3,.02) on each end face, 4 feet cyl(.06,.06,.08) under the corners, a vent grille of 5 box(.5,.03,.02) on the back face, and a hood front lip box(2.8,.06,.06) in METAL. Add a cap ring on the chimney.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-31 and -33 at zoom 9: the pots read as cooking pots, and the oven's back and side show trim and panel lines with no flat face over 0.5 m².
findings.verify_reason: The pots at decor.ts:186 are bare cyl(.16,.14,.22) with no rims, handles or lids. The oven body and hood are single rbox/box parts with no side or back trim (lunch-runtime.ts:75). lunch-models-31 shows the flat side and hood.

findings.title: Pip still shows the helmet ridge 'fin' and grey plinth soles from side and back (DR-64)
findings.problem: At zoom 9 in Lunch's power room (lunch-models-50b: front-top, side and back crops), Pip's hard hat has a raised ridge or fin on the crown that reads as a little ear or blade from the side and back. Each boot sits on a flat grey rectangular plate that sticks out beyond the boot outline. Both are exactly what DR-64 lists as 'no cat-ear helmet ridge, no plinth soles'. They read as model errors at the close camera, which players use constantly for plugging. (Pip is shared by all rooms; it is logged here because it is visible in every Lunch close-up, e.g. lunch-models-53, -57, -97.)
findings.fix: In tools/create_assets.py (the Pip builder), lower the crown ridge to a 1–2 mm raised rib that follows the dome (or remove it). Replace the flat sole plates with a rounded sole inset 5 mm inside the boot silhouette, in a darker ink-blue, not grey. Re-export the Pip asset.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-models-50b (front, side and back at zoom 9): no protruding fin on the helmet and no grey plate visible beyond the boot edges.
findings.verify_reason: tools/create_assets.py:63 builds the HelmetRidge as a box that sticks out above the dome toward front and back, and :71 adds a grey BootSole slab. In my game-camera shots the ridge shows as a fin on the hat (verify-lunch-models-03 from the back, -07 from the front), and grey plates sit under the boots (verify-lunch-models-05).

notes.models:
Overall the Lunch kit is in the right style family. It uses chunky rounded boxes (rbox/RoundedBox), toon ramp shading, ink outlines on props and fixtures, and a warm office palette. Several fixtures read well at the game camera: the oven front (window, knobs, bake dial, socket plate), the fridge (magnets, handle, live thermometer), the kitchen feed post (yellow block, bolt glyph, socket, floor conduits to the oven and storeroom lamp), the conveyor (scrolling belt, legs, teal strip-curtain flaps), the swing doors (upright, portholes, kick plates), the cleaner bots, the mop bucket (wringer, bail, mop), the wedge (rubber ribs), the bridges (ink top strip), the splitters (socket face, power lamp) and the thick-cable dolly. Confirmed fixed: the bookshelf book colours vary per row, the vending machine faces +z, and the doors stand upright. g.audit(.02) returns [] at start. At .005 it lists only 9 paper-on-desk contacts of about 1 cm, which is benign. Console and page errors were [] in every run.

The weak spots are concentrated in the last third of the job and in decor that has no physics:
- The lift reads as a floating table, Pip's head goes through it, and nothing connects the winch to it.
- The tray floats across a 3 m gap.
- A stray dark socket cube sits under the lift.
- The capacitor cart doesn't read as capacitors and has no inlet.
- Decor furniture has no colliders (benches, plants, chairs, rack), so Pip and the blobs interpenetrate them, and the audit can't see it.
- The rack has an upright through two crates and is built twice.
- Posters sit over windows and on each other.
- The vending machine, cooler, pots and the oven's back are under-detailed, and the supply-cart gauges are bare boards from behind.
- Supply cart A tips over when Pip simply walks past.
notes.clarity: Model-side clarity problems: the job-yellow colour is reused by 9 clutter crates and 12 mugs, and the clutter also has teal and white crates. That dilutes 'yellow means job item' right next to the wedge, bridges and storeroom. A dark socket box near the lift and the cap cart's missing socket give false or missing affordances. The storeroom 'darkness' is a tinted lid that still shows every crate, while the lamp shade pokes through bright, so the can't-grab-in-the-dark rule isn't sold by the visuals. The kitchen counters are office desks with keyboards, so the serving pass doesn't read as a kitchen.
notes.fun: From the models side, the room's physical comedy is helped by the bots, swing doors and splitters. It is hurt by sparse clutter: 137 props, half of them paper and mugs, with a big empty wood corridor and no lounge or beanbag clusters. That leaves little to knock over on the routes, and the climax (lift and tray) looks unfinished. Fixing the lift cage, rope and conveyor extension makes the win moment read as a machine doing its job.
notes.playability: Two model and physics issues affect play directly. First, supply cart A tips onto its side (55.9°) from an ordinary walk past and never rights itself; the respawn rule only fires above y 2.1. Second, decor without colliders lets Pip walk into benches, plants and under the lift car. Draw calls are 1257 at start and 1303 in survey (fullfx), and 1309 in lowfx, versus about 175 in PROGRESS. Most of that is unmerged shell-wall window parts on game.root, plus a lamp cord rebuilt every frame. Host fps is still 60, but the DR-24 budget is blown.
notes.teaching: The models carry some teaching well: the bake dial on the oven, the fridge thermometer and sad-food icon, the floor conduits showing the post's fixed wiring, the cart gauges, and the scorch and warning badges. But the start-up-kick lesson is undercut: the winch never visibly pulls the lift (no rope, no drum spin), and the capacitor cart has none of a capacitor's visual cues and no socket. The physical story 'feed → cart → winch → lift' therefore isn't drawn. The capCord only appears once docked, and there is nothing at the inlet.
